parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-isko via Old Polish *-isko.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian вада (vada, “flaw, slander”), the sense "'flaw'" is probably a semantic loan from Old Polish wada, from Proto-Slavic *vada. By surface analysis, ва́дити (vádyty) + -а (-a).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian вспакъ (vspak), possibly from Old Polish wspak, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *opakъ.

parole.significato: to care, to look after, to take care
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian дба́ти (dbáti), judging by its geographic spread, likely borrowed from Old Polish dbać, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *dъbati. Cognate with Belarusian дбаць (dbacʹ), Czech dbát.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian до́бре (dóbre), from Old Polish dobrze, from Proto-Slavic *dobrě, from Proto-Slavic *dobrъ. Doublet of добрі́ (dobrí). See Ukrainian добрий.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian зле (zle), from Old Polish źle, from Proto-Slavic *zъlě, from Proto-Slavic *zъlъ. Doublet of зло (zlo).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian насѣньє (nasěnʹje), from Old Polish nasienie, from Proto-Slavic *nasěnьje.

parole.significato: to destroy, to obliterate, to annihilate, to eliminate
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian нищити (niščiti, “to destroy, to devastate, to ruin, to impoverish”), possibly from Old Polish niszczyć, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *niščiti. By surface analysis, (dated) ни́щий (nýščyj) + -ити (-yty).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian осо́ба (osóba, “person, appearance, species, hypostasis”), possibly borrowed from Old Polish osoba.

parole.significato: lord, master, mister, sir (a general honorific title)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian панъ (pan), from Old East Slavic панъ (panŭ), from Old Polish pan, from Proto-Slavic *gъpanъ.
Inherited from Middle Ukrainian па́ни f sg (pány), from Old East Slavic пани f sg (pani), from Old Polish pani f sg, from Proto-Slavic *gъpanьji f sg.

parole.significato: diverse, heterogenous, multifarious, manifold, motley, various (consisting of many different elements)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian розмаи́тый (rozmaítyj), from Old Polish rozmaity, probably from unattested dialectal West Slavic *orzmaj, from Proto-Slavic *orzmajati, from *majati.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian роспачъ, роспачь (rospač, rospačʹ), from Old Polish rozpacz, from Proto-Slavic *orzpačь. Compare Belarusian ро́спач (róspač).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian скри́ня, скры́ня (skrínja, skrýnja), from Old Polish skrzynia, from Proto-Slavic *skrini, from Old High German skrīni, from Latin scrīnium.

parole.significato: to last, to endure, to continue
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian трыва́ти (tryváti), from Old Polish trwać, from Proto-Slavic *trъvàti.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian триво́жити (trivóžiti), from earlier трво́жити (trvóžiti), from Old Polish trwożyć, from Proto-Slavic *trъvožiti. By surface analysis, триво́га (tryvóha) + -ити (-yty).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тримати (trimati), from Old Polish trzymać, from Proto-Slavic *trimati.
